candidates.title: MeanFlow average-velocity identity
candidates.target_claim: Let u(z,r,t) be average velocity along the locally unique ODE trajectory ending at arbitrary endpoint(z,t), defined on a neighborhood, with fixed r and dz/dt=v(z,t). Derive u=v-(t-r)[D_z u·v+partial_t u] from the displacement integral and establish the converse with a bounded diagonal limit.
candidates.earliest_date_status: Verified date in the arXiv v1 submission history, used as a disclosure-date proxy. First public announcement time and earlier talks, code, theses, abstracts and equivalent results are unresolved; this is not a certified earliest disclosure.

primary_sources.claim_supported: v1 date and average-velocity contribution
Section 4.1 equations 4-8 and Appendix B.3; inspect boundary assumptions separately

antecedents.relationship: Flow Matching supplies instantaneous marginal/conditional velocity context.
Shortcut Models already use step-size-conditioned finite-time transport; audit whether its consistency equation or earlier transport literature contains an equivalent two-time identity.

prerequisites.A: Fundamental theorem of calculus and the product rule with a fixed integration endpoint.
prerequisites.B: Total versus partial derivatives along an ODE trajectory; average displacement divided by elapsed time.

candidates.bridge: Differentiate the displacement relation along the same trajectory while holding the earlier time fixed. The donor cue must not contain the final identity or JVP direction.
candidates.verification: Prospective proof check: differentiate the defining integral, expand the total derivative, and integrate the differential identity back. Include polynomial/nonconstant trajectories, vector fields, r=t limits, and an unbounded C/(t-r) counterexample to an unrestricted converse. Require boundedness or a boundary condition. When requesting separate partial derivatives, define the full endpoint field via the supplied locally unique ODE, including neighboring endpoints and any required branch/domain. An average specified on just one trajectory fixes only its total derivative, not individual partial derivatives.
unavailable_empirical_claims: One-step ImageNet quality, optimization stability, effectiveness of conditional-velocity substitution or stop-gradient training, and FID comparisons are not established by recovering the identity.

candidates.target_claim: Reconstruct an exact three-element comparison/copy sorting program that removes a redundant value movement under the established partial-order invariant, while preserving the multiset and ascending order for signed integers. Specify the exact instruction set and instruction-count benchmark before asserting improvement.

Existing libc++ sort kernels and older sorting-network/superoptimization literature form the comparison baseline; exact early variant and public release history require audit.

prerequisites.A: Compare-exchange/min-max operations and known partial orders after an initial comparison.
prerequisites.B: Conditional assignment, register liveness and redundant-copy elimination under path invariants.

candidates.bridge: Use the order already established by preceding comparisons to identify which conditional copy cannot affect the final sorted output; it must not supply the replacement expression itself.
candidates.verification: Prove equivalence over all total preorders of three inputs including ties, then check faithful signed comparison/conditional-move ISA semantics and register/memory behavior. A source-level compare/copy model admits a small complete checker; arbitrary C++ comparators, NaNs, UB and real assembly require additional semantics. Count instructions under a declared cost model; do not infer CPU speed.
unavailable_empirical_claims: CPU latency, library-level speed-ups, search efficiency and portability are empirical; instruction count alone does not establish the published runtime gains.
